checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does extract_deposit_data terminate with InvalidBlock on ALL validation failures?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all validation checks in extract_deposit_data (size checks for pubkey=48, withdrawal_credentials=32, amount=8, signature=96, index=8). 2. For EACH validation check, craft input that fails ONLY that specific check. 3. Trace the code path after each validation failure - verify it immediately raises InvalidBlock. 4. Search for any early returns, fallthrough logic, or silent error handling that could allow continued processing. 5. Check for exception handlers that might catch and suppress InvalidBlock. 6. Fuzz with malformed deposit data to find any code path that silently accepts invalid data. 7. Verify no logging-only error paths exist where validation failure is logged but processing continues.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Source Invariant: SG-001/INV-005, Source Threat: stride-004, Trust Boundary: tb-002. A silent validation bypass would allow malformed deposit data into the consensus pipeline, causing divergence between implementations that do and do not reject the data. Attacker can control ABI-encoded deposit data via Transaction or P2P entry points.
